newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH, LEICESTER EAGER TO SHED UNWANTED RECORDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH, LEICESTER EAGER TO SHED UNWANTED RECORDS.

text.p: Middlesbrough have never won a major trophy -- Leicester City have lost every cup final they have played at Wembley, so at least one unwanted record will go in Sunday's English League Cup Final.
Middlesbrough have famously won nothing in their 121-year history apart from the old Amateur Cup twice in the 1890s and the minor Anglo-Scottish Cup, a semi-official tournament, 21 years ago.
Now they are poised to create something of a unique, if bizarre hat-trick by becoming the only club to reach two cup finals and be relegated in the same season.

For not only are Bryan Robson's schizophrenic team through to the League Cup final, they have also reached the F.A. Cup semifinals for the first time. They are odds-on favourites to beat second division Chesterfield and make the F.A. Cup final for the first time -- but they are also fighting to stave off relegation from the premier league.
Middlesbrough have played like two different teams this season, beating the likes of Newcastle and Liverpool in cup matches, but until recently hardly able to put a foot right in league games.

On their day the Brazilian midfielders Emerson and Juninho and Italian striker Fabrizio Ravanelli have been worth every penny of the 18.0 million pounds ($29.5 million) that manager Bryan Robson and Steve Gibson, Middlesbrough's young millionaire owner, have spent on securing their services.

But when Emerson has gone missing, Juninho overwhelmed by players almost twice his size and Ravanelli spent all match moaning at the referee and his team mates, they have looked like the relegation-threatened side they have become.
Earlier this week Juninho was linked with a possible 7.0 million pounds ($11.5 million) move to Valencia in Spain, but if he does go, he would be desperate to leave with a medal -- or two.

Juninho's signing from Sao Paulo in October 1995 marked the start of a new era in the club's relatively unremarkable history -- and he says he wants to win something to prove the past is gone as far as the club are concerned.
"I didn't just come to Middlesbrough to play in the premier league," he said recently, "I wanted to win trophies, I wanted to be part of history."
Like Middlesbrough, Leicester's trophy cabinet has not exactly been bulging with silverware down the years.
Leicester's only major honour was winning the then two-legged League Cup in 1964.
Their last major final was as long ago as 1969 when they were beaten 1-0 in the F.A. Cup final by Manchester City, and, shades of Middlesbrough, were relegated the same season.
Until 1994, and again last season when they won at Wembley in the promotion play-off final, their record under the Twin Towers was renowned only because it was so bad.

They lost the 1949 F.A. Cup final there to Wolves, the 1961 final to Tottenham, the 1963 final to Manchester United and the 1969 final to Manchester City. No team has played in as many F.A. Cup finals without a victory.
Leicester have established themselves in the premier league this season and are a hard-running side based on a solid defence which breaks quickly on the counter-attack.

The match pits the tactical acumen of old playing foes Robson and Martin O'Neill and the match is likely to be evenly balanced. Leicester won 2-0 at Middlesbrough earlier in the season, while Middlesbrough beat Leicester 3-1 at Filbert Street three weeks ago.

Bookmakers Ladbrokes make Middlesbrough slight favourites at 11-8 with Leicester at 7-4. One piece of magic could win it and that could come from Juninho or Ravanelli, depending of course on whether they show their l eague, or their cup form.
